headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line while funding stays positive and fear sits at 31
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's uniform today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day moving averages. No golden crosses anywhere on the board. That's a market where the long-term trend is still down or at best flat across the whole complex, not a case of one weak asset dragging down six strong ones. BTC itself is 49% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, and ADA is the extreme case at -81.8% from its high with a 30-day realized volatility of 55.9%, roughly double BTC's 21.7%.

Momentum tells a slightly different story than trend, and that gap is worth naming. RSI readings are mostly in neutral ground: BTC at 48.6, ETH at 55.5, SOL at 52.6, BNB at 58.3, none overbought or oversold. XRP's RSI of 37.3 is the lone soft spot. MACD is split down the middle: SOL, BNB and DOGE show MACD above signal (short-term momentum turning up even while price sits under the 200-day), while BTC, ETH, XRP and ADA don't. That's a market resting rather than trending hard in either direction, with pockets of tactical strength inside a longer downtrend.

Positioning leans long and isn't cheap to hold that way. Every asset on the leverage board shows positive funding, from BTC's 5.1% annualized up to DOGE's 11.0%. Long/short account ratios confirm the crowd is stacked long: DOGE at 5.11, XRP at 3.66, SOL at 2.42, BTC at 2.03. Longs paying shorts across the board, with DOGE traders paying the most to stay in the position. Liquidations over the past 20-24 hours skew toward longs getting hurt in ETH ($5.5M in short liquidations vs $1.96M in long liquidations, meaning shorts actually took the bigger hit there) and BTC ($2.55M shorts vs $1.9M longs, same pattern). So even with a crowd leaning long, the liquidation tape shows shorts absorbing more damage in the last day, a mild disagreement between stated positioning and who's actually getting squeezed.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. BTC spot ETFs printed -$56.2M net on 14 Aug, and the five-session net is -$385.2M with three consecutive days in the same direction, a real short-run outflow trend on the traditional-finance side. ETH ETFs went the other way: +$5.9M on 13 Aug, +$46.6M over five sessions, though only two days in the same direction so call that a lean, not a trend. Whale wallets, meanwhile, moved $62.6M in BTC onto exchanges over the last 72 hours, with the single biggest onto-exchange move being $149.8M in USDT into Bitfinex, the largest line item on the whole board. That stablecoin move is dry powder showing up at an exchange, not evidence of what it'll be used for. Zooming out to the weekly whale series, the last two readings were negative (-$42.2M then -$501.7M) after two positive weeks before that (+$428.7M, +$1.154B), so the multi-week direction has flipped negative recently. Stablecoin float itself is basically flat, down 0.59% over 30 days on a $306.4B base, so the sidelines aren't visibly refilling.

Sentiment is Fear at 31, sitting in the lower half of its own 30-day range of 25 to 34, so today isn't even the fearful extreme of the past month, just comfortably within it. That reading sits oddly next to a tape where BTC is up 1.25% and the broader market cap is up 0.85% on the day. Fear during a green day, longs paying funding while shorts eat the liquidations, ETF outflows on BTC against a small inflow lean on ETH: the crowd's mood and the money's behavior aren't telling the same story right now. Worth watching from here: whether BTC's five-session ETF net turns positive again, whether the long/short ratios come down as funding cost rises, and whether the weekly whale flow prints a third straight negative week or snaps back like it did after the two prior negative-to-positive transitions.
